subject: Pilot enablement — success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@blueharbor.ai>, Marcus Jensen <marcus.jensen@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot enablement — success criteria & next steps

Hi Elena / Marcus,

Great to meet today — thanks for walking through BlueHarbor's ingestion and alerting use cases. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before we schedule the kickoff: 

Key pain points you shared:
- Latency-sensitive scoring on 1–2k requests/min across peak windows (current CPU-based service hits 400ms p95).
- High token cost for contextual reranking across long customer transcripts.
- Compliance: logs retention for 12 months and VPC-only egress for customer data.

Pilot scope (proposed):
- Duration: 4 weeks (2-week integration + 2-week eval & metrics).
- Models: open LLM base + reduced-cost quantized variant for reranking.
- Success metrics: p95 generation latency <= 150ms; rerank throughput >= 1.5k req/min; token cost reduction >= 35% vs baseline.
- Acceptance: agreed QoR on a 50-sample prompt/eval set (we'll bootstrap with the samples you shared).

Owners / roles:
- BlueHarbor: Elena (technical lead), Marcus (product owner)
- Redwood: Rishi (AM, prim contact), Ben (SE, infra/setup), Mina (CS, success metrics & evals)

Immediate asks from BlueHarbor to get started:
1) Network: allow redwood-serving-prod outbound to 52.23.44.0/24 (we'll provide exact CIDR).
2) Sample eval set: upload 50 representative transcripts to the Drive link below.
3) Compliance contacts: point person for SOC2 / legal questions.

I attached a short pilot-charter stub so we can iterate quickly. Can we target a kickoff the week of Jan 4? If that works, Ben will send a short infra checklist and Mina will circulate the evaluation template.

Thanks — I’ll update the Drive folder with the charter and a draft mutual action plan after this mail.

Best,
Rishi
--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0122
From: Elena Park <elena@blueharbor.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Jensen <marcus.jensen@blueharbor.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 12:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot enablement — success criteria & next steps

Thanks Rishi — helpful summary and aligned on most points. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Network/CIDR: we'll need the explicit outbound IPs + expected port ranges for our security team. Can Ben include that in the infra checklist?
2) Data handling: per our policy, transcripts must be stored with customer IDs pseudonymized prior to upload. I'll ask our data team to pseudonymize the 50-sample set and drop it in the Drive.
3) Compliance lead: looping in our Head of Security, Priya Kaur (priya.kaur@blueharbor.ai), she may have additional questions about retention / audit log formats.

Kickoff week Jan 4 is fine but Marcus is on leave Jan 6–8; can we do Jan 5 or Jan 9 as options? We prefer afternoons (PST).

Also — curious about the quantized variant: do you have a short note on expected quality delta vs base model? If Ben can sketch numbers that’ll help our product team.

Best,
Elena
--
Elena Park
CTO | BlueHarbor Analytics
elena@blueharbor.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@blueharbor.ai>, Marcus Jensen <marcus.jensen@blueharbor.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot enablement — success criteria & next steps

Elena — I’ll include the CIDRs and port ranges in the infra checklist. Quick technical notes to set expectations: 

- Egress/ingress: Redwood Dedicated can be set up in your VPC with customer-managed NAT — we'll provide the small set of outbound IPs (typ: 52.23.44.10–52.23.44.15).
- KV cache: for transcript context, we recommend enabling prefix caching (saves ~20–30% tokens for repeated customer IDs).
- Quantized variant: based on similar corpora we’ve seen, 4-bit quantization yields ~5–8% ROUGE-style score degradation but 2–3x cost savings for reranking. We'll run a quick A/B on 100 samples during week 2 to quantify.

Attached: network-egress-reqs-stub.txt (stub) and I'll drop the infra checklist to the Drive by EOD.

—Ben
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot enablement — success criteria & next steps

Hi all — thanks, this is shaping up well. A couple of points on evaluation & timeline: 

- Eval plan: Mina will own the 50-sample acceptance run. Proposed thresholds: latency p95 <= 150ms, rerank precision delta <= -2% relative to baseline human labels, cost <= 65% of current per-transaction token spend.
- Data: once you upload the pseudonymized set, we'll add synthetic customer ids to preserve context cadence during testing.
- Timeline suggestion:
  * Jan 5 (Wed) 1pm PST — Kickoff (preferred)
  * Jan 6 (Thu) 1pm PST — Infra validation & connectivity check
  * Jan 11 (Tue) — Baseline run + A/B quantized test starts
  * Jan 19 (Wed) — Final eval & handoff/runbook delivery

I'll draft the evaluation template (CSV + scoring rubric) and share in the Drive folder. If Jan 5 works for BlueHarbor, I'll block it on everyone's calendar and add the draft agenda.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

3) Redwood (Mina): Populate evaluation template and sample rubric — due Dec 22.
4) All: Confirm kickoff slot — Jan 5 at 1pm PST or Jan 9 at 1pm PST.

I’ve uploaded the pilot-charter-blueharbor-v0.1.pdf and a short mutual action plan to the Drive folder. Doc link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBzBlueHarborPilot (see MA P/Draft).
